Had a TeamViewer subscription for a few years; cancelling it when choosing not to renew was tedious and difficult. No longer recommends TeamViewer, calling it "janky as hell."

User says TeamViewer sends a reminder email 30 days before expiry, but unless you cancel at least 30 days ahead, it auto-renews and demands a full year's payment under threat of legal proceedings. Feels the email lulls you into thinking you can just let it lapse.
Uses TeamViewer on one gaming PC only to log into Windows and start Steam after Wake-on-LAN over a home VPN, then plays via Steam Remote Play. Looking for an alternative, ideally OSS and self-hosted.
Used TeamViewer less than twice a month to help elderly relatives, yet TeamViewer kept killing connections, treating them as a professional abusing the free tier. Now looking for an alternative.

Explains the installed font's purpose: the get.teamviewer.com invitation page checks via JavaScript (fontdetect.js) whether the TeamViewer font is installed. If found, it launches the app through the teamviewer8:// protocol handler; otherwise it prompts a download.

Commenter argues storing saved passwords with reversible encryption in the user's registry hive is unavoidable for a client that must replay them. Suggests the Windows Data Protection API would be a modest improvement, but says user-context attackers could bypass it anyway.
Says the real problem isn't the lack of hashing but that low-privileged users can access the stored TeamViewer credentials.
Has seen recommendations to move away from TeamViewer for years: it was once good and free, but casual users can now use Chrome Remote Desktop and more technical users Splashtop.
TeamViewer worked well until it flagged non-commercial family IT support as commercial. Tried their unflag process, gave up, and is now happy with AnyDesk.
Incident responder says they found compromises tied to TeamViewer's stored credentials. Wrote code to enumerate them en masse and analyze TeamViewer connection logs; calls the results "eyepopping."
Says the product seemed full of security flaws from first use, with poorly implemented desktop sharing, and calls it "no wonder it is a favourite of scammers."

"TeamViewer works very well, but the company is a bit scummy and the pricing is crazy." Compares it to Windows RDP plus Tailscale (works well), PulseWay (barebones and slow), and open-source VNC tools (disappointing).
Tried RustDesk as a TeamViewer alternative to help their dad, but it refused to install on his older macOS version. Supported OS versions weren't clear from the website.

Complains you can't install TeamViewer on Mac without admin permissions even just to control another desktop, unless you manually extract the .app from the .pkg. Also questions the lack of end-to-end encryption between connected computers.

An Australian retail bank locked the user out of online banking, using TeamViewer's presence as one signal in flagging a suspicious transaction. Notes TeamViewer no longer seems to be detected via the font.
Scam-baiter videos show most scammers use TeamViewer, yet the commenter says TeamViewer does little to nothing to make it harder for scammers.
